requirements.title: Processors may provide halting control with processor-dependent mechanics
requirements.definition: Some processors allow control over aborting or continuing after an exception through IEEE_SET_HALTING_MODE; halting is imprecise after the exception, and the initial halting mode is processor dependent.

pending.halting-occurrence-imprecise: No portable oracle fixes termination point or mechanism after a halting exception; fixture authors must not run with halting .TRUE. as a conformance expectation.
pending.initial-halting-mode-processor-dependent: No portable oracle fixes the initial halting mode. Future fixtures must set halting .FALSE. for a supported flag before observing preservation.

requirements.oracle:
Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first, use conforming single-image programs, and assert only portable Clause 17 properties: named derived-type values, exact logical results, exact type/kind/rank characteristics, supported IEEE special-value classifications, exact representable arithmetic under the named support inquiry, or get/set round trips. Unsupported guarded branches are skips, not passes. Processor-dependent support availability, NaN payloads, exact halting mechanics, initial modes, approximation latitude, and IOMSG text are not asserted.

S17.6-001 halting-control fixture: on a profile requiring IEEE_SUPPORT_HALTING(IEEE_OVERFLOW), SET_HALTING_MODE(...,.FALSE.) followed by GET_HALTING_MODE observes .FALSE.; no initial mode or precise halting occurrence is asserted.

Optional IEEE facilities are gated by tests/profiles that require the supported branch before the fixture runs; no unsupported-success branch is counted as coverage. Processor-dependent initial modes, IEEE_OTHER arithmetic effects, decimal-real behavior absent from the host, halting occurrence timing, performance latitude, status-object internals, and reference-compiler failures of procedure-return mode restoration remain pending.

Unregistered dependencies explicitly retained: the remaining Clause 17 procedure descriptions, IEEE derived types and named constants, processor support inquiries, exception-flag semantics, rounding-mode semantics, and ISO/IEC 60559 terminology.

requirements.title: Procedures preserve halting mode except the halting and status setters
requirements.definition: A procedure other than IEEE_SET_HALTING_MODE or IEEE_SET_STATUS does not change the halting mode on entry and ensures the same halting mode on return.

pending.procedure-return-restores-halting-mode: Guarded branch plan: probe IEEE_SUPPORT_HALTING(IEEE_OVERFLOW); supported branch sets halting .FALSE., calls an IEEE_EXCEPTIONS procedure other than IEEE_SET_HALTING_MODE or IEEE_SET_STATUS, and asserts the post-call halting mode equals the pre-call mode; unsupported branch records skip.

accounting.rationale: Mixed processor latitude and halting-mode preservation are split into fine units.
Processor support for halting control is permitted, not required.
Halting timing after an exception is processor latitude.
The initial halting mode is processor dependent.

review_rationale: Batch309 bound reference-validated IEEE fixtures after one review round; frozen-LFortran failures (rounding modes ineffective, non-logical IEEE_SUPPORT_* results, missing IEEE_MODES_TYPE) were independently confirmed as genuine.
